summary.headline: [ERROR] AD Domain Controller configuration issue: GSSAPI/Kerberos requires hostnames, not IPs.

config_findings.message: Kerberos SPN Risk: 'ad_server = 192.168.1.10' is configured as an IP address instead of a hostname. Kerberos (GSSAPI) requires hostnames to request tickets.

sssd_config_snippet:
[sssd]
domains = example.com

[domain/example.com]
id_provider = ad
ad_server = 192.168.1.10
krb5_realm = OTHER.NET
ldap_uri = ldap://dc.other.net
problems: No nameservers found in /etc/resolv.conf. DNS resolution will fail.
No active Time Synchronization service found. Kerberos/AD requires synchronized time.
PAM configuration does not include pam_sss.so. SSSD authentication will not be triggered.
No Kerberos Keytab (Machine Account) principal found. AD join might be broken.
Kerberos SPN Risk: 'ad_server = 192.168.1.10' is configured as an IP address instead of a hostname. Kerberos (GSSAPI) requires hostnames to request tickets.
warnings: [TUNING] If AD users authenticate but fail authorization (missing groups), consider setting 'ldap_use_tokengroups = False'.
[TUNING] No LDAP timeout specified. Adding 'timeout = 30' can help stabilize slow Active Directory connections.
[DIAGNOSTIC HINT] SSSD debug level is low. To get better logs, set debug_level=9 in sssd.conf, restart sssd, reproduce the error, and generate a new supportconfig.
